	Contract Abstract Info	Terms	Contract Term	Add Item, Save Changes, Delete Item, Import Data, Audit Log, Printable View, Save to Documents, Link	Purpose: Defines the core structure and classification of the specific lease period.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			Key Data Points:																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Term Definition: Captures Term Number, Term Type (e.g., Initial, Renewal), and Term Status.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Space Metrics: Records Rentable Area and Area Unit (e.g., Square Feet).																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Financial Reference: Includes Option Rent PSF (Per Square Foot).																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Document Reference: Links specific clauses to the physical lease document (Document Name, Section, Page).																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms	Key Dates	(Same as above)	Purpose: Manages critical timelines, milestones, and notification windows associated with the contract term.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			Key Data Points:																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Date Classification: Key Date Group, Type, and specific Action definitions.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Duration: Begin Date and End Date of the specific date logic.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Notice Management: Tracks Earliest/Last Notice Periods, Notice Begin/End Dates, and flags for "Notice Sent" or "Notice Received."																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Actions: Tracks Action Dates and completion status ("Is Action Complete?").																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms			- Contingencies: Defines trigger events or contingencies linked to these dates.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Terms	Key Date Notes	(Same as above)	Purpose: Provides a free-text area to capture qualitative details, specific instructions, or context regarding the dates that do not fit into the standard structured fields.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Amendments	Listing and Detailed View	(Same as above)	View contract amendments list with details | Add/Edit/Delete  amendment row with classification and details with text description summarizing key changes and save | Attach supporting documents for the amendement | Use amendments in downstream processes  when configuring workflows or reporting. | Kick off Workflow routing for amendments | Amendment‑driven reporting updates 																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Covenants	Convenants Listing | Add/Edit items | Add/Edit ASC 842 fields | Add/Edit Key dates | Notes	(Same as above)	Covenants Listing – Grid showing all covenants on a contract (group, type, status, document/section/page) so users can quickly scan and select items to work on.​ | Add/Edit items – Form for creating or updating covenant headers, including group/type/status, document references, and abstracted covenant language, then saving back to the list.​ | Add/Edit ASC 842 fields – Section where users maintain accounting details (covenant amount, adjustment type, linked ASC 842/IFRS schedules, RVG amounts, allocation, currency) that feed lease‑accounting calculations.​ | Add/Edit Key dates – Controls for defining covenant dates (coverage period, notice window, ticklers, frequency, completion flags) which automatically create and update Key Date records and alerts.​ | Notes – Free‑text areas used to capture explanations, negotiation history, or special handling instructions that supplement the structured covenant and key‑date data.																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Key Dates	(Same as above)	(Same as above)	(Same as above)																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Responsibilities	(Same as above)	View responsibilities list | Add/edit responsibility line | Record section reference | Capture comments	Responsibilities list grid – Shows each maintenance category and identifies which party must maintain, repair, and replace it, with a reference to the lease section. | ​ | Add/Edit responsibility – User adds or selects a row, picks the maintenance category, assigns landlord/tenant/both for maintain/repair/replace from dropdowns, enters the section reference, and saves																						
	Contract Abstract Info	Insurance	(Same as above)	Add, Edit, delete insurance policy information of a contract	The Insurance tab stores insurance policies for a contract, with fields to capture: insurance group/type/category, policy number, policy dates, required/insured flags, certificate request/received dates, coverage limits (total and single‑occurrence) with currency, comments, responsible contact, and links to the related covenant, section, and amendment.

These standard covenants could be applied to their contracts on a global level at implementation, but the customer could indicate that the covenant does not currently exist on a specific contract by clearing the Covenant Exists? check box. Then, when it is time for the customer to renegotiate the contract, they can quickly and easily see which covenants should be negotiated in the new contract. 			ExpenseVendorAllocation.PaymentPercentage	Payment Percentage	True	Enter the allocation percentage in this field.  Your vendor allocations must total 100%. However, if two vendors are entered with both vendors having an allocation of 100%, both vendors will be paid 100%. Allocations are processed in order from largest to smallest. The smallest allocation will receive what remains of a payment. This means that it is very important that vendor allocations are entered correctly. For example, if two vendors have been entered as having a 60-50 split when the allocation should have been 50-50, the first vendor would be paid 60%, while the second would be paid 40%. If a vendor allocation does not exist, transactions will still be generated with an empty Vendor field. Any changes to the vendor allocation will set current and future expense schedule statuses to Review. They will need to be approved using the Approvals Process procedures.	Enter the allocation percentage in this field.  Your vendor allocations must total 100%. However, if two vendors are entered with both vendors having an allocation of 100%, both vendors will be paid 100%. Allocations are processed in order from largest to smallest. The smallest allocation will receive what remains of a payment. This means that it is very important that vendor allocations are entered correctly.
